Today: 2026-10-05
Brightfin Games studio weekly - Monday 5 October 2026. Focus project this week: Lantern Isle 1.4 "Tides" content update (release target October 15 on Steam and Switch). Other teams' sections follow.

Lantern Isle 1.4 - production notes
Content is locked. The update adds the Saltmarsh region, eleven new quests, the fishing-net crafting chain and the long-requested co-op save sharing. Localization into nine languages came back from the vendor on September 28; the Polish and Brazilian Portuguese teams fixed 63 string overflows in the quest log over the last week. Audio is final, although Mateus wants to remix the storm ambience in a later patch because it masks footsteps.

Community and marketing
The trailer went up on September 30 and has 410,000 views. Wishlist additions on Steam are 2.3 times the rate we saw before 1.3. Hana is lining up three streamers for launch week. Press kit is ready except for final Switch screenshots, which need the certified build.

Platform submission
The Switch build was submitted for platform certification on September 24 together with the Steam release candidate review. Certification came back on October 2 with a fail: a save file can corrupt if the console sleeps during an autosave, which is a mandatory fix. The fix is in progress and the resubmission is planned for October 9; with the platform's standard turnaround, the earliest Switch release is October 27, and the publisher wants both platforms to launch together, so October 15 is off for Steam as well. Hana is moving the store pages to October 27.

QA
Remaining known issues are minor: a fishing net that clips through the dock in one camera angle, and a tooltip that shows the wrong stack size for kelp. Neither is a release blocker by our criteria. Sasha's team switches to compatibility testing on the Steam Deck this week.

Other teams
- Project Ember (new IP prototype): the publisher pitch has slipped from October 20 to November 10 because the vertical slice needs another combat pass.
- Mobile port of Lantern Isle: the porting partner is waiting on the publisher to approve the revenue split before it can start. Nothing to do on our side yet.
- VR experiment "Driftwood": cancelled after the playtest on September 29; motion sickness scores were too high. The two engineers move to Ember.
- Tools team: the new level-streaming editor plugin shipped internally on Friday.

Studio operations
Office heating maintenance on Wednesday morning; the second floor will be cold until noon. Payroll moves to the new provider in November; HR will send instructions. Reminder that the quarterly all-hands is on October 22.

Hiring
Two offers accepted: a senior gameplay programmer for Ember and a community manager who will support Hana from November. The technical artist role remains open.

Shout-outs
Thanks to the localization pod for absorbing the late string changes, and to Ines for rebuilding the crash reporter dashboards in a weekend.

Next week's report will be compiled by Hana.

Today: 2026-11-20
Merriam University Library - Research Data Services team meeting, 20 November 2026. Main project in these notes: Hollis, the open research-data repository funded by the Clearwater Foundation grant. Other library projects are covered in the round-up.

Attendees: Fiona Gallagher (head of research data services), Omar Siddiqui (repository developer), Bettina Krause (metadata librarian), Leon Achterberg (systems), Ruth Okonkwo (grants office).

1. Hollis: development update
Omar demonstrated the deposit workflow end to end: a researcher uploads a dataset, fills in the metadata form, receives a DOI and can set an embargo. Large-file upload (up to 200 GB through resumable transfers) now works on the test system. The integration with the university's research-information system pulls author details automatically, which researchers in the pilot liked. Remaining work is the curation queue for librarians, usage statistics, and the accessibility audit.

2. Hollis: metadata
Bettina finished the mapping from our schema to DataCite 4.5 and to the national aggregator's harvesting format. She tested harvesting with the aggregator's sandbox and the records came through cleanly, including funder identifiers. She is now drafting the depositor guidance pages.

3. Hollis: grant and timeline
Ruth reported on the Clearwater Foundation. The grant's original end date is December 31, 2026, and the public launch was promised for that date. Because two developer positions were vacant for most of the spring, we asked in October for a no-cost extension. The foundation approved the extension on November 16: the award now ends on April 30, 2027, and the public launch is re-planned for March 2027, with the curation queue and usage statistics finished in January and the accessibility audit in February. Omar and Bettina continue on the current work plan without interruption; the extension only moves the end date, not the budget.

4. Hollis: pilot feedback
Twelve research groups tested deposits in October. The most common request was for a way to deposit code alongside data; Omar suggested linking to the university's GitLab rather than storing code in Hollis. Two groups from chemistry asked for larger embargo periods for patent reasons; Fiona will check the policy.

5. Round-up of other library projects
- Digitisation of the Ellery manuscript collection: the scanning vendor is three weeks late; new completion date January 12.
- Discovery-layer replacement: the procurement was cancelled in September because no bid met the accessibility requirements; it will be re-tendered next year.
- Reading-room booking app: waiting for IT security to approve the single sign-on configuration before it can go live.
- Thesis deposit mandate: the graduate school confirmed it starts in February.

6. Systems
Leon reported that the storage array for Hollis has 61 percent of its capacity free after the pilot. Backups run nightly to the second data centre and a restore test passed on November 9. He will renew the TLS certificate for the test system next week.

7. Any other business
Fiona reminded everyone that the library closes from December 23 to January 2. Holiday cover for the research-data inbox is posted on the team calendar. Bettina will present the metadata work at the regional repository forum in January.

Actions
- Omar: finish the curation-queue design and share it with Bettina.
- Bettina: publish the depositor guidance draft for comment.
- Fiona: answer the chemistry groups on embargo length.
- Leon: renew the test TLS certificate.

Next meeting: 4 December 2026.

text:
今天：2026-06-04
ADR-017：站內搜尋的後續技術路線
所屬專案：Kestrel（自建全文搜尋引擎，2025 Q4 啟動）
決策日期：2026-06-02　決策者：CTO 王志豪、架構委員會（5 票同意、1 票棄權）

背景
Kestrel 的目標是用 Rust 自建倒排索引與排序服務，取代現行的 MySQL LIKE 查詢，原訂 2026/07/31 交付 v1，支援商品、文章、店家三種索引。截至 5 月底，索引建置與基本查詢已能運作，但中文斷詞、同義詞、拼寫校正與相關性調校都還沒開始，團隊估計至少還要兩季。
同一期間，資料平台組完成了託管 OpenSearch 的評估：在 3,000 萬筆商品資料上 p95 查詢延遲 85ms，中文分析器與同義詞功能現成可用，每月費用約 NT$18 萬。

考慮過的選項
1. 繼續 Kestrel，並增聘 2 名搜尋工程師：成本最高，而且年底前仍達不到商用品質。
2. Kestrel 縮小範圍，只做商品索引：大約 9 月可交付，但維運負擔仍全在我們身上。
3. 停止 Kestrel，改用託管 OpenSearch。

決策
採用選項 3。Kestrel 自 6/2 起終止，不再開發，原定的 v1 搜尋服務不會交付，repo 轉為唯讀封存。站內搜尋改由新成立的「OpenSearch 導入」專案負責，該專案由資料平台組主導，另訂時程與預算。

後果
- 正面：每季省下約 4 人月的開發與維運人力；搜尋品質可望在第三季改善。
- 負面：既有的 Rust 索引程式碼與基準測試工具不再維護；對託管服務商產生依賴，合約中須寫入資料匯出條款。
- 人員：Kestrel 的三位工程師，兩位轉入 OpenSearch 導入專案，一位回推薦系統組。
- 硬體：兩台 64 核索引主機於 6/20 前歸還機房，改撥給 log 平台。

附記
架構委員會同場也討論了推薦系統的 feature store 選型（ADR-018，下次會議再決議），以及 API gateway 的升級時程，兩者與本 ADR 無關。

City of Eastbrook - Digital Services Steering Committee, minutes of the meeting held 2 April 2026. Primary item: the Permit Portal v2 project (online building and trade permits), which is the project these minutes record decisions for. Other agenda items are summarised after it.

Members present: Deputy City Manager Lorraine Whitfield (chair), CIO Marcus Feld, Building Official Teresa Quan, Finance Director Bill Andersson, Council liaison Councilmember Rosa Delgado. Staff: project manager Kevin Osei.

Item 1 - Permit Portal v2: status report
Kevin summarised progress since January. The contractor has delivered the applicant account module and the fee calculator, both of which passed user-acceptance testing with the permit counter staff. The inspection-scheduling module was about 40 percent complete. Spend to date is 612,000 of a 1.4 million budget.

Item 2 - Permit Portal v2: state mandate
The CIO reported that the governor signed House Bill 2217 on March 20. From January 2027 every municipality in the state must accept building and trade permit applications through the state's shared ePermit system, and locally built portals may not take applications after that date. Teresa confirmed that the state system covers all of Eastbrook's permit types and that the state funds the onboarding. After discussion, the committee voted 5-0 to terminate Permit Portal v2. The contractor's statement of work will be closed at the end of the current billing period on April 15, the inspection-scheduling module will not be completed, and the portal will not be launched to the public.
